observation.visible_scene: A daytime sky: a deep blue field with a large, layered gray-and-white cumulus/stratocumulus bank occupying the lower-left and left third, a faint diagonal cirrus band stretching across the right half, scattered small wisps near the top, and a low horizon line of small clouds at the bottom-right.
visible_changes: A small, distinct white cumulus puff near the top-center of the frame drifts steadily downward through the middle of the scene over the excerpt (from the top edge in the early frames to roughly the vertical center by the last frames).

The left cloud bank slowly changes shape and position: additional bright white cloud mass grows into the upper-left corner, and the bank's right edge protrusion shifts modestly, indicating slow lateral/vertical drift of the low cloud layer.
The diagonal cirrus band on the right and the bottom horizon clouds remain largely fixed in position relative to the frame throughout the excerpt.
A few isolated tiny dark specks appear in single frames (e.g., upper-left early, center mid-clip), not persisting across frames.
outside_clip_unknowns: The wind field and cloud motion before t=0 and after the clip ends are not visible.
Whether the left bank will continue to advance or dissipate beyond this segment is unknown.
uncertain_details: It is uncertain whether the apparent motion is purely cloud drift or partly camera movement; the top puff moves downward while the right cirrus stays put and the left bank moves in a different direction, which is more consistent with real wind-driven drift of different cloud layers than with a single camera pan.
The identity of the brief dark specks (possible birds or sensor noise) is unconfirmed since each appears in only one frame.
